attacksRun.attack: prefix exactly at the operative bound dropped or first-authored
attacksRun.evidence: Retained in whatIsNotAuthored ('CC-5 prefix exactly at the operative bound' and 'CC-5 prefix exactly at the postHandshake bound'), in remainderAfterThisCorpus ('remains unauthored, including its postHandshake half'), in registerRowNote, in proposedLaterWork[4], and in findingDisposition.namedOpenDecision. whatIsAuthored states 'Prefix exactly at the operative bound is not authored.' doesNot and failsIf both guard first-authoring.

controlFrameEncoding.note states 'The quoted preHandshake clause refuses N greater than 65536 or N equal to 0; N=65536 is not that refusal.' doesNot carries 'Does not pin N=65536 as prefix-only RF-2.' The named tension is preserved rather than settled: registerRowNote attributes the open decision to the quoted preHandshake clause and CC-5 intent disagreeing about N=65536. Verified against the live contract: transportAndFraming.framing.bounds.preHandshake refuses N greater than 65536, so N=65536 exactly is not refused from the prefix alone, while the closed CC-5 intent lists prefix exactly at the operative bound as an RF-2-typed injection. The tension is real and is correctly left open.

attacksRun.attack: N=1 treated as newly invented rather than quoted from the 4-byte unsigned encoding
attacksRun.evidence: authorityClaim, whatIsAuthored, member.mutation and basedOn.controlProtocolV2.role all derive N=1 as the minimum positive value of the quoted 4-byte big-endian unsigned length encoding at control-protocol-contract.v2 transportAndFraming.framing.frame, selected to avoid inventing a constant. The frame clause is quoted verbatim and resolves to the live JSON pointer .transportAndFraming.framing.frame. The predecessor first-authoring g21-fixture-corpus.v26 (D-352, dual ACCEPT 0/0) used the identical derivation for the same constant, so the justification is lineage-consistent, not novel.

attacksRun.attack: 0x80 treated as a newly invented protocol bound rather than a quoted UTF-8 continuation octet
attacksRun.evidence: authorityClaim, controlFrameEncoding.note and member.mutation all state 0x80 is a UTF-8 continuation octet that cannot start a well-formed UTF-8 sequence, quoted from UTF-8 well-formedness and not invented as a protocol bound; failsIf carries the prohibition explicitly. Verified on the bytes: 0x80 lies in the continuation range 0x80-0xBF and is an invalid UTF-8 start byte, so the body is not a UTF-8 JSON text as required by the verbatim-quoted controlFrameEncoding.encoding (RFC 8259).

member.mutation states 'Body length 1 equals claimed N=1, so this injection is not truncated-body'; whatIsAuthored, authorityClaim, expected, doesNot and failsIf all repeat the distinction. Verified on the bytes: N parses to 1 and the body is exactly 1 octet, so body length equals claimed N and the frame is complete. Occupancy EV-5 oversize-from-prefix correctly does not apply, since the live EV-5 exactByteIntent scopes that behaviour to CC-5 oversize and N=1 is neither 0 nor greater than 65536; the corpus correctly states the receiver must read the body.

The D-352 truncated-body member at docs/coop/artifacts/fixtures/g21.v22/G21.cc5.truncated-body.bin is 4 bytes, 00000001, digest b40711a8…; this payload is a distinct 5-byte file, 0000000180, digest ad8cb54a…, at a distinct path, witnessing a distinct property (body length equal to N with a body that is not well-formed UTF-8, versus fewer than N body bytes). The shared leading four octets are the forced big-endian encoding of N=1, which both corpora quote from the same transportAndFraming.framing.frame clause; they are not a re-pin of the authored truncated-body member. whatIsNotAuthored, doesNot and failsIf each guard reuse of those bytes, and the guard holds.
